title: Right kidney and its hilum (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: On the back wall of the abdomen behind the peritoneum, from about T12 to L3. The right kidney lies a little lower than the left.
Filters the blood and makes urine; controls water, salts, acid-base balance, and blood pressure; makes erythropoietin and activates vitamin D.
Renal artery from the aorta. The renal vein drains into the inferior vena cava.
hy: The left kidney is preferred for transplantation from a living donor because its renal vein is longer.
A horseshoe kidney is held low in the abdomen because it is caught under the inferior mesenteric artery as it ascends.

rows: Funnel-shaped upper end of the ureter at the hilum of the kidney. It lies behind the renal vein and artery.
Collects urine from the calyces of the kidney and passes it into the ureter.
hy: The junction of the renal pelvis and the ureter is the most common site of obstruction of the urinary tract before birth.

rows: Muscular tube about 25 cm long that runs from the renal pelvis down the back wall of the abdomen, crosses the pelvic brim near the division of the common iliac artery, and enters the bladder.
Carries urine to the bladder by waves of contraction.
hy: It passes under the uterine artery in women and under the ductus deferens in men (water under the bridge) and can be injured when the uterine artery is tied in a hysterectomy.
Kidney stones lodge at its three narrow points: the junction with the renal pelvis, the pelvic brim, and where it enters the bladder.

rows: Side of the aorta at about L1 to L2, just below the superior mesenteric artery.
The right artery is longer and passes behind the inferior vena cava. At the hilum each artery lies behind its renal vein.
Kidney, with small branches to the suprarenal gland and the ureter.
hy: Renal artery stenosis causes hypertension through renin release. It is due to atherosclerosis in older adults and to fibromuscular dysplasia, typically in young women.

rows: Kidney. The left vein also receives the left suprarenal and left gonadal veins.
Lies in front of the renal artery. The left vein is longer and crosses in front of the aorta just below the superior mesenteric artery.
hy: The left renal vein can be squeezed between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta (nutcracker syndrome), causing flank pain, blood in the urine, and a left varicocele.
The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein and the right one directly into the inferior vena cava, which is why a varicocele is usually on the left.

rows: On the upper pole of each kidney.
Cortex, from outside in: aldosterone (zona glomerulosa), cortisol (zona fasciculata), androgens (zona reticularis). Medulla: epinephrine and norepinephrine.
Superior, middle, and inferior suprarenal arteries. The right suprarenal vein drains into the inferior vena cava and the left into the left renal vein.
hy: The layers of the cortex and their products, from outside in: salt, sugar, sex.
The medulla develops from neural crest cells; a pheochromocytoma is a tumor of its chromaffin cells.

rows: Lower limbs, pelvis, abdominal wall, kidneys, suprarenal glands, gonads, and liver. It is formed at L5 by the two common iliac veins.
Ascends on the right of the aorta and behind the liver and passes through the diaphragm at T8.
hy: Levels of the openings in the diaphragm: inferior vena cava at T8, esophagus at T10, aorta at T12 (I ate ten eggs at twelve).

rows: Continues the thoracic aorta as it passes through the diaphragm at T12.
Descends in front of the lumbar vertebrae, on the left of the inferior vena cava, and divides at L4 into the two common iliac arteries.
Three unpaired branches to the gut (celiac trunk, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric arteries) and paired branches to the suprarenal glands, kidneys, gonads, and body wall.
hy: Abdominal aortic aneurysms usually lie below the renal arteries. The main risk factors are smoking, age over 65, male sex, and hypertension.
